desc:
Given an array nums of positive integers and an integer k, count the non-empty subsets of positions whose sum is divisible by k. Positions are what matter, so equal values at different positions give different subsets. Return the count modulo 1,000,000,007.

nums = [1, 2, 3], k = 3  -> 3   ({3}, {1, 2} and {1, 2, 3})
nums = [4, 4], k = 2     -> 3   ({4}, {4} and {4, 4})
hints: Going through all 2<sup>n</sup> subsets is too slow for n = 2,000. What matters about a subset is only its sum modulo k.
Process the elements one at a time and keep, for each remainder r, how many subsets of the elements so far have sum mod k equal to r.
When an element x arrives, every subset with remainder r can either skip it or extend to remainder (r + x) mod k. The empty subset is counted at remainder 0, so subtract one at the end.
editorial: Let dp[r] be the number of subsets, the empty one included, whose sum leaves remainder r modulo k. It starts as dp[0] = 1. For each element x the new table keeps every old subset and also adds, for each old remainder r, a copy shifted to (r + x) mod k.
After all elements are processed, dp[0] counts the subsets with sum divisible by k, including the empty set. Subtracting one gives the non-empty answer, reduced modulo 1,000,000,007.
The work is O(n * k) with n up to 2,000 and k up to 60, comfortably fast. Only remainders are stored, so the subset sums themselves can be large without trouble.
